Question: Pass journal entries for: (a) goods purchased on credit from Ram for Rs 20,000; (b) cash paid to Ram Rs 15,000 in full settlement after a discount of Rs 500.
reference_answer: (a) Purchases A/c Dr. 20,000; To Ram 20,000. (b) Ram Dr. 20,000; To Cash 15,000; To Discount Received 500; To Balance c/d 4,500. The unpaid balance is carried forward.
keywords: journal entries, credit purchase, discount received, settlement, ledger

Question: Prepare a trial balance from the following balances: Capital Rs 1,00,000; Cash Rs 25,000; Debtors Rs 30,000; Creditors Rs 15,000; Sales Rs 80,000; Purchases Rs 60,000; Rent Rs 5,000.
reference_answer: Debit balances: Cash 25,000 + Debtors 30,000 + Purchases 60,000 + Rent 5,000 = 1,20,000. Credit balances: Capital 1,00,000 + Creditors 15,000 + Sales 80,000 = 1,95,000. The given data are incomplete; a suspense or missing account must reconcile the difference.
keywords: trial balance, debit, credit, capital, purchases, sales

Question: Calculate depreciation for three years on machinery costing Rs 5,00,000 using the straight-line method at 10% per annum.
reference_answer: Annual depreciation = 5,00,000 x 10% = Rs 50,000. Depreciation for three years = Rs 1,50,000; book value after three years = Rs 3,50,000.
keywords: depreciation, straight-line method, cost, useful life, book value

Question: Explain the profit-sharing ratio and treatment of goodwill when a new partner is admitted into a partnership.
reference_answer: The new partner is admitted with a agreed share; old partners sacrifice in their old ratio unless otherwise agreed. Goodwill brought by the new partner is credited to the sacrificing partners in their sacrifice ratio. Revaluation and capital adjustments are recorded separately.
keywords: partnership, admission, profit-sharing ratio, sacrifice ratio, goodwill
